l4_steps.name: Ingest corporate lead from partner referral
l4_steps.input: Lead referral from GDS TMC partner, NDC API inquiry, or inbound web form
l4_steps.output: New lead record created in Salesforce with source, contact, and estimated spend
l4_steps.kpi: Lead response time ≤4 hours; lead conversion rate ≥25%
l4_steps.pain_point: Leads arriving via multiple channels (Sabre PRISM, direct email, NDC API) have no unified ingestion point — manual entry causes data gaps and delayed response

l4_steps.name: Score and qualify lead by spend threshold
l4_steps.input: Lead record with estimated annual air spend and company size
l4_steps.output: Qualified or disqualified lead; assigned lead score (0–100)
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce lead scoring models are not calibrated against actual ticket revenue data from Amadeus Altéa PSS, resulting in mis-scoring of high-value accounts

l4_steps.name: Assign qualified lead to regional sales rep
l4_steps.input: Qualified lead record with territory and vertical segment
l4_steps.output: Lead assigned to named sales rep with SLA clock started
l4_steps.kpi: Assignment turnaround ≤2 hours; SLA acknowledgement by rep ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Territory alignment rules in Salesforce are manually maintained and lag behind network route changes, causing mis-assignment of accounts near new city-pair launches

l4_steps.name: Create opportunity record and discovery call
l4_steps.input: Assigned lead record; initial client discovery meeting notes
l4_steps.output: Salesforce opportunity with Stage = Discovery, estimated ARR, and travel policy details
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales reps manually key in travel volume data from client spreadsheets; no API integration with SAP Concur or Egencia to import actual managed travel spend

l4_steps.name: Model fare & volume proposal with RM inputs
l4_steps.input: Client O&D mix, estimated annual seat volume, preferred travel windows
l4_steps.output: Draft corporate fare proposal with negotiated discount tiers and volume thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal margin ≥ target contribution per O&D; average corporate discount ≤14% off published fare
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue Management team must be consulted manually for each proposal; no self-service fare modelling tool for sales reps, causing bottlenecks when RM team is capacity-constrained

l4_steps.name: Submit proposal for RM and pricing approval
l4_steps.input: Draft fare proposal; RM contribution model output
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected proposal with RM sign-off recorded in Salesforce opportunity
l4_steps.kpi: RM approval turnaround ≤48 hours; approval rate on first submission ≥70%
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflow is email-based with no SLA enforcement; pricing decisions are lost outside Salesforce audit trail, creating compliance risk under ATPCO corporate fare filing rules

l4_steps.name: Submit approved proposal to corporate client
l4_steps.input: RM-approved fare proposal; client contact details
l4_steps.output: Formal proposal document sent to client; opportunity stage updated to Proposal Submitted
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal acceptance rate ≥55%; time-to-response from client ≤7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal documents are generated from Word templates rather than CRM-native output, leading to version mismatches and unapproved fare terms being quoted

l4_steps.name: Negotiate corporate agreement terms with client
l4_steps.input: Submitted proposal; client counter-proposal or negotiation notes
l4_steps.output: Revised term sheet with agreed discount levels, volume commitments, and bonus triggers
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle time ≤10 business days; concession rate (additional discount) ≤3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiation concessions (extra discount, waived change fees) are granted ad hoc without systematic tracking, eroding yield across the corporate portfolio without visibility to Finance

l4_steps.name: Execute contract and record in CRM
l4_steps.input: Agreed term sheet; legal corporate agreement template
l4_steps.output: Executed contract stored in Salesforce; opportunity stage = Closed Won
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution time ≤3 business days post-agreement; 100% of contracts stored in Salesforce with expiry date populated
l4_steps.pain_point: DocuSign / e-signature integration with Salesforce is not enforced; some reps email PDF contracts outside CRM, breaking the audit trail and renewal reminder automation

l4_steps.name: Load negotiated fares into PSS and GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with agreed fare levels, booking codes, and validity dates
l4_steps.output: Corporate fare records loaded in Altéa and filed to Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and Amadeus GDS via ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: Fare load accuracy 100%; time from contract execution to fare availability ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual fare loading into Altéa and ATPCO filing are separate processes with no automated handoff from Salesforce contract record, creating a window where the corporate account is active but fares are not yet bookable

l4_steps.name: Configure corporate account in booking tool and TMC
l4_steps.input: Corporate account ID, negotiated fare codes, TMC contact details
l4_steps.output: Account configured in Sabre PRISM with correct preferred fare hierarchy; TMC notified
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy rate ≥99%; TMC test booking success rate 100% before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM configuration must be done separately from Altéa PSS fare loading; mismatches between the two systems cause TMC booking failures that are only discovered by the corporate traveller

l4_steps.name: Activate corporate account and confirm with client
l4_steps.input: Confirmation from Distribution Ops that fares are live and booking tool is configured
l4_steps.output: Account activation confirmation email to client; Salesforce account status = Active
l4_steps.kpi: Time from contract execution to account activation ≤3 business days; activation CSAT ≥4.2/5
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated trigger from Altéa or Sabre PRISM back to Salesforce to confirm fare go-live; sales reps manually chase Distribution Ops, delaying client communication and eroding trust in the onboarding process

l4_steps.name: Track corporate booking volume against contract targets
l4_steps.input: Booking data from Amadeus Altéa PSS; contract volume commitments from Salesforce
l4_steps.output: Monthly account scorecard showing actual vs target volume by O&D and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: Volume attainment ≥90% of contracted threshold; on-time scorecard delivery by 5th of each month
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa booking data is not directly piped into Salesforce opportunity tracking; reporting requires manual extracts and reconciliation in Tableau, introducing a 5–7 day data lag that slows account intervention

l4_steps.name: Conduct quarterly business review with corporate client
l4_steps.input: Account scorecard; market share data from Sabre PRISM; competitive benchmarks from OAG
l4_steps.output: QBR presentation delivered; action items logged in Salesforce; contract amendment flags raised if needed
l4_steps.kpi: QBR completion rate 100% for accounts >$500K ARR; action item close rate ≥80% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG market share data and Sabre PRISM share-of-wallet reports are not integrated into Salesforce, requiring manual assembly of QBR materials and reducing time available for strategic client discussion

l4_steps.name: Assess contract renewal or renegotiation trigger
l4_steps.input: Contract expiry date alert; YTD volume attainment; competitive win/loss signals
l4_steps.output: Renewal decision: auto-renew, renegotiate, or let expire; opportunity stage updated accordingly
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal rate ≥85% for accounts meeting volume thresholds; renewal initiated ≥90 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce contract expiry alerts are often suppressed or ignored; accounts have lapsed without renewal, forcing expensive re-acquisition through GDS channels at higher distribution cost
